coverage: ECB public supervisory sanctions (including NCA sanctions published on the ECB register at the ECB's request). Excludes other national-authority sanctions, unpublished or deferred decisions and enforcement outside prudential banking supervision.
executive_summary: During 2026, the EU banking framework moved from Basel III implementation to targeted recalibration. CRD VI national transposition was due by 10 January, while the Commission recorded incomplete implementation in several Member States, including Austria. In June, the Commission adopted temporary FRTB relief, published in September and applicable from January 2027. Its July banking competitiveness Communication followed a February–April consultation and signalled legislative proposals for early 2027. EBA consultations meanwhile advanced SREP coordination, operational-risk governance, supervisory reporting and credit-risk standards. ECB supervision emphasised resilience, asset quality and geopolitical risks. Pending proposals remain non-binding; adopted measures require distinct legal application-date tracking.

outlook.summary: Capitalisation and profitability remain robust, while asset-quality pockets, geopolitical spillovers and increasingly connected non-bank exposures warrant granular monitoring. This is a sector-level outlook, not a bank-specific compliance or credit rating.

themes.title: Credit quality / CRE / SMEs
themes.text: Aggregate NPLs remain low, but CRE, SME and consumer credit exposures require granular monitoring; ECB Q2 2026 SME NPLs rose quarter-on-quarter.

themes.title: Geopolitical and energy shocks
themes.text: EBA points to second-round energy-cost and sectoral impacts. ECB's 2026 reverse stress test identified weaknesses in some banks’ internal stress-testing frameworks.

themes.title: Non-bank links / private credit
themes.text: EBA reports rising exposures to non-bank financial institutions and concentration in larger banks. Look through correlated exposures and valuation practices.

themes.title: Capital reform / output floor
themes.text: EBA’s CRR3/CRD6 dashboard estimates a 15.1% fully loaded CET1 ratio for its sample and a greater output-floor effect than in the preceding edition.

themes.title: Funding resilience
themes.text: Funding and liquidity remain robust but market repricing and competition for stable funding could constrain planned balance-sheet growth.
